pluss::timeline::now¶

Back to Timeline Factory API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline pluss::timeline::now()

Capture One Absolute Instant¶

now() reads the system clock once and returns that reading as a rank-zero, one-element Timeline with UTC timezone metadata. It is the direct choice for a measurement boundary, event timestamp, or reproducible cutoff captured at the call site.

There is no local-versus-UTC argument. An instant is absolute; changing a timezone changes only its civil representation. Use tz_convert() when the same captured instant should be displayed in another zone. Use today() when the desired value is a calendar midnight rather than the current instant.

Example 1: Verify The Clock Capture¶

Dynamic examples must test bounds rather than claim a fixed timestamp:

const auto before = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
    std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();
const auto observed = pluss::timeline::now();
const auto after = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
    std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();

const auto tick = observed.epoch_nanos().item<std::int64_t>();
std::cout << (observed.dim() == 0 && observed.numel() == 1 &&
              observed.tz() == "UTC") << '\n';
std::cout << (before <= tick && tick <= after) << '\n';

Output¶

true
true

The bound assumes the system clock is not adjusted backward between the three reads, which is the same operational limitation as any wall-clock timestamp. now() is not a monotonic elapsed-time clock.

Example 2: Capture Once When Consistency Matters¶

const auto batch_time = pluss::timeline::now();
const auto opened_at = batch_time;
const auto audit_time = batch_time;

std::cout << opened_at.eq(audit_time).item<bool>() << '\n';

Output¶

true

Two separate calls are two separate clock reads and normally differ. Reuse one captured scalar when multiple records must carry an identical boundary.

Example 3: Project The Same Instant For Display¶

const auto captured = pluss::timeline::now();
const auto local_view = captured.tz_convert("America/Edmonton");

std::cout << (captured.epoch_nanos().item<std::int64_t>() ==
              local_view.epoch_nanos().item<std::int64_t>()) << '\n';

Output¶

true

The timezone conversion changes wall-clock fields and formatting, not the captured epoch nanoseconds.

See Also¶

  • moment: resolve now with an optional fixed elapsed offset.

  • today: resolve a UTC or process-local calendar midnight.

  • format: produce shaped text from a captured Timeline.
